name: 41. Cross-Provider Content-Block Cache Control & cachePoint (#5629)
description: Extends folder 40's Bedrock-invoke coverage of the reviewer comment on invoke.go:808 across the other places Bifrost surfaces prompt caching. Bedrock Converse-native cases (/converse, /converse-stream) prove cachePoint on a plain content block and nested inside a toolResult's own content produce real cache hits when the client speaks Converse's native wire format directly (no cache_control translation involved — Converse-shaped input was already unaffected by the invoke-route fix per folder 40's regression guard; these cases pin the downstream caching pipeline itself, live, mirroring folder 40's model/streaming/multi-tool-call coverage). Azure gets one write/read pair proving automatic (marker-free) prefix caching, since Azure OpenAI shares OpenAI's caching mechanism exactly (no content-block/tool_result distinction applies there). Vertex-hosted Claude and native Anthropic (/anthropic/v1/messages) both get the same two scenarios as folder 40 (plain content-block and nested-tool_result cache_control) using their own genuine Anthropic-dialect wire format -- Vertex-Claude's usage surfaces through the unified /v1/chat/completions route in OpenAI-shape (prompt_tokens_details.cached_tokens), while native Anthropic returns its own snake_case usage fields directly. OpenAI itself is intentionally not duplicated here -- Cross-Cut Round 31 already has strong write/read prompt-caching coverage for it, and OpenAI's caching is fully automatic prefix-matching with no cache_control/cachePoint marker concept, so there's no content-block-specific angle to add. OpenAI itself is also covered here, structurally analogous to the other providers' two scenarios even though OpenAI's caching is fully automatic prefix-matching with no cache_control/cachePoint marker: one write/read pair primes/reads the cache from a large non-system content block (Round 31 and the existing 'system reuse' backlog case only exercise the system-message case), and a second pair does the same across a full tool-call turn whose tool result is the large prefix, the structural counterpart to every other provider's nested-tool_result scenario in this folder.
